I was taken in by the Vetolympe clinic after my cat had an accident. I had just been to two other veterinary clinics, one of which was mediocre. I arrived there in utter despair, not knowing if my cat would survive. But he did, we both survived, and with tremendous support from the clinic, without which I wouldn't have made it. Their support didn't end with the consultations. It was there before and after. They did a wonderful job, truly. With respect and kindness throughout. They take the time to answer the same questions several times during their incredibly busy days. My cat had another operation, and it was the same story. They have become my go-to vets; I entrust them with the care of all four members of my household without hesitation. Total confidence; for me, they are truly humane vets who love animals above all else. And a special mention for Dr. Ballade, whom I particularly admire!

Hello Elodie,

Thank you for your excellent feedback and for the trust you placed in our team.

The Vet Olympe Veterinary Team

A huge thank you to the entire medical team for their warm welcome, gentleness, attentive listening, and boundless patience. The staff stayed well past closing time to see us, and we received the results very quickly. We left feeling completely at ease. This is a veterinary clinic that truly goes the extra mile, and you can feel their passion for their work. Thank you again from the bottom of our hearts, from the whole family and from Onyx!
Excellent. Our vet takes perfect care of my little Chihuahua. The vet is gentle and professional with her. I highly recommend this clinic.

Never go there! The receptionists are incredibly unpleasant and utterly incompetent. They answer coldly and treat you with disdain, especially for emergency appointments. The vets are afraid of cats. My cat was near death, and the only thing they could suggest was paying for a CT scan or MRI, without even trying to relieve my cat's pain. I had asked them to ease his suffering because I could see he was in agony. There was absolutely no gentleness; my cat was terrified and wouldn't let anyone near him. They claimed my cat was already dead, lol. They only know how to take money. They anesthetized my cat unnecessarily with a tranquilizer that completely paralyzed his body. They didn't even give him an IV or an anti-inflammatory or anything to ease his pain. My cat had soiled himself, and they left him bathing in his own urine. You pay 300 bucks to be told your companion is going to die, and on top of that, they leave him to bathe in his own urine.
I wouldn't recommend this clinic to anyone. Personally, I won't be going back. They're incompetent! My cat died in terrible pain. And these vets just want to make you pay for treatment so their profits increase—it's a disgrace! I'll never bring my animals back to you again! I'll tell everyone about you, you bunch of incompetents and scammers!

I greatly appreciated the time Dr. Lecru took to answer all my questions and provide an accurate diagnosis for my pet. Finally, a veterinarian who listens, takes the necessary time, and doesn't make you feel rushed. I recommend her without hesitation.

I can't thank the entire team at Vet Olympe Clinic enough.

For the past week, they have been fighting every day to save my cat, Pompi. During such a difficult time, they have demonstrated exceptional professionalism, but above all, immense compassion.

The whole team is incredibly kind, gentle, and attentive. They take the time to cuddle Pompi, reassure him, and care for him with so much love. As an owner, it's a huge comfort to know my pet is in such good hands.

They have given me updates very regularly, sent me photos, and always taken the time to answer my questions and reassure me. You can tell they deeply love animals and do everything they can to provide them with the best possible care.

I especially want to thank Dr. Capdeville, who is an exceptional veterinarian. Her professionalism, attentiveness, availability, kindness, and dedication to Pompi touched me deeply. She never gave up and always sought the best solution for him. I will be eternally grateful.

Thanks to the entire team, Pompi was able to receive prompt care and is now benefiting from all the treatment he needs. I will never forget everything you have done and continue to do for him.

A huge thank you to all the veterinarians, veterinary nurses, and the entire team at Vet Olympe. You practice your profession with passion, dedication, and so much heart. It is so rare to meet such compassionate, attentive, and dedicated people.

Thank you so much for everything you do for Pompi. You are extraordinary. ❤️🐾
Highly competent veterinarians who love animals. One of them saved my 2-month-old bulldog who had a heart defect; I can't thank him enough. He's almost 4 years old now.

My dog ​​receives osteopathic treatment from Dr. Couston, which allows him to continue walking despite his advanced age of 15. He also saw Dr. Ballade, who fitted him with a pin 9 years ago, which is still holding up well. The care from these two veterinarians allows him to enjoy a long and happy old age.

An impeccable veterinary clinic. The telephone reception, the reception staff—everything was perfect. The veterinarian listened attentively to my dog's concerns and gave me excellent advice. I thank the entire team.
Top-notch clinic and exceptional vet; my cat is seen by Clarisse, who is a wonderful person.

Incompetent and disrespectful. My dog's teeth cleaning was done poorly (his back teeth are black on both sides of his jaw), and the vet told me that if I wasn't happy with the result, I could just go somewhere else! Then, she ended up asking me to pay a second time for the service that wasn't performed before yelling at me to leave! Avoid at all costs!

I arrived 30 minutes before closing time with my dog, who was vomiting blood and whose condition seemed very worrying.
I was told that no treatment was possible at that time and that I would have to wait for the emergency clinic next door to open, 30 minutes later.
Given my dog's condition, I preferred to go immediately to the Massilia veterinary emergency clinic in Saint-Barnabé, where he was finally seen. During the journey, he continued to vomit blood and pieces of his stomach (confirmed by the veterinarians).
Fortunately, his condition stabilized afterward.
I understand the time constraints, but in a situation I perceived as a life-threatening emergency, this refusal to treat him was extremely difficult to accept.
This will therefore be my first and last experience at this clinic.

The veterinarians and staff were very caring. They treated the animal gently and kindly, and listened attentively to the owners.

Thank you for your care.

This is my second visit; the reception is pleasant, the assistants are gentle and caring with our pets.

The veterinarians are professional and handle our companions with great care.

I removed one star because I don't believe it's possible to have a designated vet.

The clinic is very clean.

Dr. Saban is brilliant. Avoid Dr. Le Balleur; she's actually an ophthalmologist who practices general medicine. We found her to be dishonest and incompetent. She couldn't answer our questions and became irritated whenever we tried to understand our cat's condition. She missed important details, and this doctor is very disappointing. Just so you know, don't leave your pet overnight; there's no staff to look after them. Money is clearly a driving force at this clinic.

It's a veterinary center. At first, I was worried because the team is large, and you always think it's better to have one vet than several. I went there three years ago because I had some problems with my usual vet. Since then, I haven't changed because the care is perfect, and the center has specialists, so the file is on-site and the specialists can communicate with each other. The equipment is also very complete... Everything is done on-site.

Review posted 2 years ago:
My dog ​​was very sick for a month. We took her to several vets who prescribed medication, but nothing helped; she just kept getting worse. From the very first consultation, Vet Olympe diagnosed lymphoma. We finally knew what she had. She was prescribed a chemotherapy and immunotherapy protocol over several months. Today, she is in complete remission, and her lymph nodes have shrunk. We can breathe a sigh of relief. A huge thank you to Dr. Derré, whom I call Dr. House, and to Ms. Lescaudron, without whom my dog ​​might not be here anymore. I highly recommend this veterinary clinic. They are truly passionate about animals and their work. They are the best.

Thank you, Laura Zarifian, for taking the time to leave this review. Even without a comment, this sign of trust means a great deal to us, and we are happy to care for your pet.

The Vet'Olympe Team

Thank you to the veterinary assistant Elsa who took care of Perlinette post-op with kindness and gentleness, to Dr. Debette as always (for 25 years!), and to Dr. Isnard who checked in the next day. 💙🩷 Exceptionally disappointed by two other veterinary assistants...🤐🙄 …

The vet was unfriendly and had an unpleasant way of answering my questions. I clearly felt like I was bothering them by asking questions, even though it's perfectly legitimate to want to understand what's wrong with your pet.

My regular vet had already performed an ultrasound, which found nothing. Despite this, the clinic insisted on doing another one, which ultimately proved useless. So I paid for an ultrasound unnecessarily.

Later, I was told that further investigation was needed with a biopsy under general anesthesia, because the samples taken under ultrasound were supposedly of poor quality. So I trusted them and paid €1,200 for this biopsy, only to learn that my dog ​​was simply suffering from a temporary liver condition.

This could have been treated with medication, as I had suggested during the initial consultation.

I felt I was dealing with a clinic that prioritizes financial gain over animal welfare, charging for very expensive medical procedures that did not seem necessary.

The reception was excellent. My little dog was cared for with great gentleness and kindness. Dr. Saban, a highly competent surgeon, took the time to thoroughly explain the condition, the different possible operations, their costs, and the recovery process. Communication with my regular veterinarian was very smooth and responsive.

I was admitted on Monday without seeing the vet, and the surgery was scheduled for the same day. Before the operation, I was told that during the first ultrasound, it would have been possible to use an endoscopy to remove the object, but during the second ultrasound that afternoon, the object was found to be in the intestine, so they had to open the stomach (which is more dangerous and expensive). Then, during the estimate (before the surgery), I was told it would cost between 900 and 1000 euros in total. I explained that I wouldn't be able to afford it all and that I needed help spreading out the payments. The response was, "This isn't a bank." Because of my love for my pet, I obviously agreed to the surgery; I had no choice, otherwise it would have been fatal.

I did manage to get a payment plan of up to four months (the standard option). Then, luckily, Tuesday was a public holiday, so the clinic was closed, and I left on Wednesday without seeing the vet (I spoke to him briefly on the phone that morning to be told everything was fine). The final cost was €1025 (the estimate was between €900 and €1000). I picked up my pet on Wednesday evening and was told she was in great shape and eating very well.
Upon arriving home, the animal isolated herself and was very unwell.
The next day, my cat had a fever of 39.8°C and still wasn't eating anything, even though she was supposed to be doing well. I called, and they asked me to come back the following morning for another ultrasound and the possibility of another operation... I was already distraught seeing my pet like that... I reiterated that I couldn't afford everything at once, and that's when the vet said, "If you want to keep her at home like this, you can." Basically, if I want, I can let my pet die. The least they could have done was say that before getting alarmed, a simple consultation would have sufficed. So I went back to my vet, and indeed, no ultrasound or further surgery was needed!

I wouldn't say the clinic in general is bad, because everything can vary from one vet to another.
In the end, my original vet, who was compassionate, helped me afterward; he even offered me the three post-operative consultations free of charge, even though he didn't owe me anything.
For me, it's a profession where you have to deal with all kinds of people. In this case, your clients at Roucas Blanc don't necessarily have the same resources as those in your current area. You have to understand that you can't just throw €1,000 around or try to add extra tests as easily as saying hello. Having a profession that involves working with people, I understand that you can't accept everything from clients, but having a minimum of compassion and humanity, especially towards a living being, is what makes you a good person and, above all, a good doctor.

Furthermore, while your prices are higher than other veterinarians (for example, a consultation costs €41 compared to €35 elsewhere, an ultrasound costs €150 compared to €75 elsewhere, and anesthesia costs €75 compared to €43 elsewhere), the price of the operation is not something to complain about. It is a surgical procedure, and I understand that its price reflects the nature of the work, even though, from what I understand, this operation could have been avoided if it had been performed after the initial ultrasound.

When I picked up my pet, I felt pressured into buying more. I had a cone, and they were determined to give me another one. I even hesitated over the cat food that my vet ultimately recommended.

I felt like I was being forced into a corner, given the circumstances, and I have the impression that they were taking advantage of my distress... it was an unbearable experience.
I still want to thank you for the surgery that saved my cat, but otherwise, it seems that not everyone can afford to have their pet treated at your clinic.

A very positive experience at this veterinary clinic. The welcome was warm, caring, and reassuring.

A huge thank you to Dr. Oger, who treated my 17-year-old cat with great gentleness and professionalism. She was able to make a clear diagnosis and carefully perform the necessary examinations.
